title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant E

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant E - Part 1.1 (theme family: technology and communication). Level A1-A2. Scored items 1-3 (the three together are scored 0-5). Three short personal questions, asked one after another. The candidate has 30 seconds to answer each question. There is NO preparation time. The examiner reads the opening words aloud exactly as written, then asks the questions one by one, timing each answer and stopping the candidate at 30 seconds.

questions.q:
CEFR MULTILEVEL MOCK - SPEAKING - VARIANT E - PART 1.1 (items 1-3, level A1-A2)

[EXAMINER: read the following aloud, word for word, at a natural pace.]

"Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[EXAMINER: play the chime, then ask Question 1. Start timing when the candidate begins speaking. Allow 30 seconds for each question. When 30 seconds have passed, say "Thank you" and move on immediately. Do not add extra prompts, do not rephrase the question and do not comment on the answers.]

QUESTION 1 (30 seconds)
"What kind of phone do you use, and how long have you had it?"

[EXAMINER: 30 seconds. Then: "Thank you."]

QUESTION 2 (30 seconds)
"Who in your family do you send messages to most often, and what do you usually write about?"

[EXAMINER: 30 seconds. Then: "Thank you."]

QUESTION 3 (30 seconds)
"What do you like doing on the internet in the evening?"

[EXAMINER: 30 seconds. Then say: "Thank you. That is the end of the first set of questions." Move straight on to Part 1.2.]
questions.topic: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant E - Part 1.1

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant E - Part 1.2 (theme family: technology and communication). Level B1. Scored items 4-6 (the three together are scored 0-5). Two pictures on one theme are shown to the candidate. The three questions are asked one after another. Question 4 (compare the two pictures) = 45 seconds. Questions 5 and 6 (personal opinion, justified) = 30 seconds each. There is NO preparation time. The pictures are described in square brackets in the script: the examiner either shows matching photographs on screen or in the Test bazasi picture slot, or, if no photograph is available, reads the bracketed description aloud slowly once before the question.

questions.q:
CEFR MULTILEVEL MOCK - SPEAKING - VARIANT E - PART 1.2 (items 4-6, level B1)

[EXAMINER: place the two photographs in front of the candidate, or display them on screen. If no photographs are available, read each bracketed description aloud once, slowly, before asking Question 4.]

[PICTURE 1: a small rural post office with wooden shelves behind the counter; an elderly man in a grey jacket is standing at a high desk writing a letter by hand on a sheet of lined paper, a stamped envelope and a pot of pens beside his elbow, warm afternoon light coming through a dusty window, nobody else in the room.]

[PICTURE 2: the inside of a crowded city bus in the evening; a teenage girl in a school uniform is sitting by the window holding her phone at arm's length on a video call, wearing white earphones and smiling at the screen; the window behind her is full of blurred street lights and other passengers are pressed close around her.]

[EXAMINER: read the following aloud, word for word.]

"Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"

QUESTION 4 (45 seconds - compare and describe the two pictures)
"What do you see in these pictures? Compare the two photographs and say how the two ways of keeping in touch are different."
[EXAMINER: play the chime. The candidate has 45 seconds. Start timing when the candidate begins speaking. At 45 seconds say "Thank you" and move on.]

QUESTION 5 (30 seconds - opinion, justified)
"Which of these two ways of keeping in touch do you think feels more personal, and why?"
[EXAMINER: 30 seconds. Then: "Thank you."]

QUESTION 6 (30 seconds - opinion, justified)
"Do you think people will still write letters by hand in twenty years' time? Why, or why not?"
[EXAMINER: 30 seconds. Then say: "Thank you. That is the end of part one." Remove the photographs and move on to Part 2.]

[EXAMINER REMINDER: no preparation time is given anywhere in Part 1.2. Do not explain the pictures, do not name the objects in them for the candidate, and do not ask any follow-up questions of your own.]
questions.topic: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant E - Part 1.2

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant E - Part 2 (theme family: technology and communication, abstract angle). Level B2. Scored item 7 (0-5). ONE picture and THREE questions are presented to the candidate AT ONCE. The candidate has 1 MINUTE of preparation and then 2 MINUTES to answer all three questions together. The candidate is NOT required to describe the picture - the picture only evokes the theme. The examiner may give the candidate paper and a pen for notes during the preparation minute.

questions.q:
CEFR MULTILEVEL MOCK - SPEAKING - VARIANT E - PART 2 (item 7, level B2)

[EXAMINER: read the following aloud, word for word.]

"Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph."

[EXAMINER: display the picture now, or read the description aloud once, slowly.]

[PICTURE: a warm kitchen in the evening with a family of four sitting round a dinner table; the food on the plates has not been touched; the father is reading something on a laptop propped against a jug, the mother is holding a phone close to her face, the teenage son is scrolling with one hand and eating with the other, and the youngest child is watching a cartoon on a tablet standing against the fruit bowl; nobody is looking at anybody else and nobody is speaking.]

[EXAMINER: show the three questions to the candidate on screen or on the question card, and read all three aloud once, in order, before the preparation minute begins. Tell the candidate that describing the photograph is not required.]

THE THREE QUESTIONS (the candidate answers all three together):
1. Tell me about a time when you used technology to say something important to someone, or to sort out a problem at a distance. What happened?
2. How has being contactable at almost any hour affected the way you rest, concentrate, or spend time with the people around you?
3. What do you think most influences how much time people in general spend looking at their screens?

[EXAMINER: "You now have one minute to think about your answers." Time exactly 60 seconds in silence. Do not speak during the preparation minute. The candidate is not required to describe the picture and does not have to mention it at all.]

[EXAMINER: at the end of the minute say "Your minute is up. Begin speaking when you hear this sound." Play the chime. The candidate has 2 MINUTES for all three questions together. Do not interrupt, do not prompt and do not re-read a question. At 2 minutes say "Thank you. That is the end of part two."]

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant E - Part 3 (theme family: technology and communication, debatable statement). Level C1. Scored item 8 (0-6). The candidate sees ONE topic statement with two lists beside it - FOR and AGAINST, three points in each. The candidate chooses TWO points from EACH list and gives a balanced argument representing both sides of the topic. 1 MINUTE preparation, 2 MINUTES speaking. The examiner may give paper and a pen for the preparation minute.

EXAMINER NOTE - OFFICIAL SCORING OF THE WHOLE SPEAKING PAPER. There are eight scored items across the four parts. Items 1-3 (Part 1.1) are scored together, 0-5. Items 4-6 (Part 1.2) are scored together, 0-5. Item 7 (Part 2) is scored 0-5. Item 8 (Part 3) is scored 0-6. MAXIMUM RAW SCORE 21. The raw score is then converted to a rating out of 75.

OFFICIAL RAW SCORE TO RATING CONVERSION: 21=75, 20.5=73, 20=71, 19.5=69, 19=67, 18.5=65, 18=64, 17.5=63, 17=61, 16.5=59, 16=57, 15.5=56, 15=54, 14.5=52, 14=51, 13.5=50, 13=49, 12.5=47, 12=46, 11.5=45, 11=43, 10.5=42, 10=40, 9.5=39, 9=38, 8.5=37, 8=35, 7.5=33, 7=32, 6.5=30, 6=29, 5.5=27, 5=26, 4.5=24, 4=23, 3.5=21, 3=19, 2.5=17, 2=15, 1.5=13, 1=11, 0.5=10, 0=0.

questions.q:
CEFR MULTILEVEL MOCK - SPEAKING - VARIANT E - PART 3 (item 8, level C1)

[EXAMINER: read the following aloud, word for word.]

"Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[EXAMINER: display the topic and the two lists, or read them aloud once, slowly and clearly, in the order printed below.]

TOPIC:
"Everyone should be required to use their real name and a verified identity on social media."

FOR (the candidate chooses two):
1. Anonymous accounts make it easy to abuse, threaten and harass other people with no consequences.
2. People write far more responsibly when their own name is attached to what they publish.
3. Fraud, impersonation and organised fake-account campaigns become much easier to trace and to stop.

AGAINST (the candidate chooses two):
1. Anonymity protects the people who need it most - whistle-blowers, survivors of abuse, and critics of powerful institutions.
2. Real names do not in fact prevent cruelty; a great deal of aggression online is already posted under people's own names.
3. Verification hands an enormous store of confirmed personal data to private companies that may lose it, sell it or be forced to hand it over.

[EXAMINER: "You now have one minute to prepare your argument." Time exactly 60 seconds in silence. Do not explain the points, do not suggest which ones to choose and do not answer questions about the topic.]

[EXAMINER: at the end of the minute say "Your minute is up. Begin speaking when you hear this sound." Play the chime. The candidate has 2 MINUTES. Do not interrupt and do not prompt, even if the candidate pauses. At 2 minutes say "Thank you. That is the end of the test."]

[EXAMINER MARKING REMINDER: item 8 is scored 0-6. Credit the choice of two points from each list, a genuine balance between the two sides rather than an argument for one side only, and reasoning on the abstract issue rather than a retelling of the printed points. The raw score for the whole paper is out of 21; convert it to a rating out of 75 using the table in the instructions above.]
